idea: Analyst-grade China channel checks for Western funds
pain: Western funds cannot verify what Chinese suppliers and customers actually say
v1: One commissioned channel-check report on a named supply chain
channel: Her fund network on the demand side, father's network on the supply side
verdict: Uses both sides of her network at once; execution friction and slow cycles are the drag.

why.distribution: Demand side is her own network; supply side depends on her father's contacts, which is a hop.
why.demand: Expert networks charge heavily for exactly this, so a paid substitute demonstrably exists.
why.fmf: She knows what a fund needs from a channel check; she is not herself the on-the-ground researcher.
why.revenue_structure: Project work, repeat with the same funds but each engagement sold fresh.
why.defensibility: Access is the moat and it is genuinely hard to replicate from a standing start.
why.leverage: Pure project labour with heavy coordination; nothing scales without hiring.
why.capital: Travel, translation, local researchers: £2-10k before first payment.
why.time_to_revenue: Sourcing local capacity and a first client: 3-6 months.
why.tailwind: Real interest in China verification, offset by rising geopolitical and compliance friction.
why.ceiling: £12k x 15 projects = £180k, and 15 cross-border projects part-time is already a stretch.

ceiling_arithmetic: £12k x 15 projects = £180k gross, less 30-40% to local researchers and translation = £110-125k net. Delivery capacity binds well before demand.
carries: Both networks used at once, high price point, and genuinely scarce access.
kills: Labour leverage and the direct-cost deduction. Also real compliance exposure on Chinese data.
test: Ask three funds whether they would commission a £10k check, and separately whether her father's contacts can source two researchers.
test_pass: One fund names a supply chain it wants checked.
test_fail: Funds say their expert network already covers it.
